answer:
REPORTED ANSWER — AIC = 111.812 (111.81 to 2 dp; exact 111.812460)

Logistic regression of treatment response (Efficacy == 'PR' -> 1, SD/PD -> 0) on BMI alone, statsmodels GLM Binomial (logit link), n = 80 complete cases, k = 2 (intercept + BMI slope), AIC = -2*logLik + 2k.

FITTED MODEL
  logit P(PR) = -3.631934 + 0.167746 * BMI
  intercept: se 2.159334, z -1.682, p 0.0926
  BMI      : se 0.097869, z  1.714, p 0.0865  (OR = 1.1826 per 1 BMI unit)
  logLik = -53.906230; deviance 107.8125; null deviance 110.8535

AIC ACCOUNTING (your point 3)
  hand-computed  -2*(-53.906230) + 2*2 = 111.812460
  statsmodels res.aic                = 111.812460
  |difference| = 0.000e+00  -> AGREEMENT CONFIRMED (script raises SystemExit if it ever exceeds 1e-6, so a silent mismatch is impossible)
  Slope-only k=1 variant would be 109.812 — explicitly NOT the reported answer; k=2 including the intercept is used and stated in the output.

MLE SANITY CHECKS (your point 4) — the fit is a genuine interior optimum
  IRLS converged = True, 4 iterations.
  Score X'(y-mu) at the optimum = max |4.6e-13| (essentially zero).
  Fitted probabilities range 0.351490 to 0.670997 — all 80 strictly inside (0,1), so no quasi-separation from BMI alone; coefficients are finite, not diverging.
  Calibration by BMI quartile (observed vs mean fitted): 18.0-19.9 -> 0.381/0.387; 19.9-22.35 -> 0.421/0.475; 22.35-23.8 -> 0.667/0.558; 23.8-25.9 -> 0.579/0.639. Overall observed PR rate 0.5125 = mean fitted 0.5125 exactly (logit property). Trend is monotone increasing in BMI as the positive coefficient implies; quartile wobble is small-sample noise, not misfit.
  Independent cross-check with a hand-coded binomial negative log-likelihood optimised by scipy BFGS (no statsmodels anywhere in that path) reproduces beta = (-3.631921, 0.167746), logLik = -53.906230 (|diff| 1.8e-11), AIC(k=2) = 111.812460. So the number is a property of the likelihood, not of the library.

CONTEXT ONLY (the single extra fit you authorised)
  Intercept-only null: logLik -55.426772, k=1, AIC 112.854.
  Likelihood-ratio chi2 = 3.0411 on 1 df, p = 0.0812; delta AIC = -1.041; McFadden pseudo-R2 = 0.0274. BMI is a weak, marginally non-significant predictor here; the question asks only for the AIC, which is 111.812.

SENSITIVITY (NOT THE REPORTED ANSWER) — printed under its own heading in the script
  primary  PR vs not-PR (SD+PD)   n=80 events=41  logLik -53.9062  AIC 111.812  <-- REPORTED
  alt      PR+SD vs PD            n=80 events=58  logLik -45.3882  AIC  94.776
  alt      PR vs PD only          n=63 events=41  logLik -38.8513  AIC  81.703
  AICs across different outcome definitions are not comparable to each other (different dependent variables), so these lines are only a demonstration of how much the coding assumption matters. The reported answer is unaffected.

SCOPING GUARANTEES (your points 1 and 2)
  No model containing Groups was fitted — kept as a code comment and echoed in output (Group 1 = 41/41 PR, Group 2 = 0 PR -> perfect separation). No covariate/context model with Age/Gender/etc. was fitted. BMI entered raw and untransformed: no standardisation, no splines, no interactions. Design matrix is exactly [intercept, BMI].

LIMITATIONS
  * The headline number is conditional on the coding assumption y = PR vs not-PR (no 'CR' exists in the data, so PR-vs-not-PR and PR+CR-vs-rest coincide; a "disease control" reading would give 94.776 instead).
  * n = 80 because the other 41 rows of the sheet are entirely blank padding, not partially observed data — nothing was imputed and no usable row was lost.
  * The BMI effect is not significant at 0.05 (p = 0.0865); the AIC is a good point estimate but the association is weak, and no model-selection claim is implied by the 1.04 improvement over the null.
  * The reported AIC uses k=2 with the intercept, the statsmodels/R glm convention.

payload.outcome_coding: y = 1 if Efficacy == 'PR' else 0 (SD and PD -> 0)
